answers.reason: Charran is the Greek NT spelling of Haran in ACT 7:2,4. Both records share G5488 and refer to Harran.
Ish-tob (H382) in 2SA 10:6,8 is commonly understood as 'men of Tob,' referring to the land of Tob known from JDG 11:3,5.
Alternate spelling of the Oak of Weeping where Deborah was buried, GEN 35:8. Both records share H439.
Apharsites (H670) are a people listed in EZR 4:9. None of the candidates represents that people.
H775 denotes Arphaxad/Arpachshad, Shem's son in GEN 10:22, and potentially his associated territory. It is unrelated to Arpad (H774), Arad, or the other candidates.
Ashdoth-pisgah (H798) denotes the slopes of Pisgah, as in DEU 3:17 and JOS 12:3. The slopes are a specific geographic feature rather than the mountain or peak represented by pisgah.
Ashurites (H805) names a people in Ish-bosheth's realm, 2SA 2:9, whose identification is disputed. It does not identify the city Asshur (H804) or either other candidate.
Bajith (H1006) occurs in ISA 15:2 in the Moab oracle, interpreted as a place or temple. None of the candidates is an established equivalent.
Beth-ham-Merchak (H1023) is the 'far house' where David stopped while leaving Jerusalem, 2SA 15:17. None of the candidates denotes that location.
Baale-Bamoth (H1181) denotes the 'lords of the high places' of Arnon in NUM 21:28. None of the listed candidates represents that designation or its referent.
